chunks: Return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing Him.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be 'well-pleased and well-pleasing' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as addressing the faithful soul generally, though some scholars specify it refers to the Prophet's daughter, Fatimah al-Zahra (peace be upon her), highlighting her unique status. The dual states of *raḍīyah* (contentment with divine will) and *marḍiyyah* (divine pleasure) underscore the culmination of the believer's journey through trials, reflecting the Shia emphasis on patience and love for the Ahl al-Bayt as a path to divine satisfaction.
